# phdscanner.com API

Search and browse PhD opportunities and professor postings from PhDScanner.com

## Install / import

```python
from parse_apis.phdscanner_com_api import PhDScanner
```

## Operations

Call these on the client's collection accessors (e.g. `client.<collection>.<op>(…)`) or via active-record navigation on returned objects — see [`example.py`](./example.py) for the exact call spelling. List operations return a lazy `Paginator`.

| Call | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `client.opportunities.get(opportunity_id: str)` | `Opportunity` | Get full details of a single PhD opportunity by its ID, including the complete HTML description, supervisor contact information, and application details. |
| `client.opportunities.search(country: Optional[str] = None, funded: Optional[Funded \| Literal['true']] = None, university: Optional[str] = None, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Opportunity]` | Search PhD opportunities with optional filters for country, university, and funding status. Returns paginated results sorted by most recent. Each result includes title, university, location, discipline, supervisor, funding details, and an AI-generated summary. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.postings.list(limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Posting]` | List PhD position postings shared by professors on LinkedIn. Returns professor details, university, department, and the post content. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |

## Errors

| Error | Raised when | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `OpportunityNotFound` | The opportunity ID does not exist or has been removed | `opportunity_id` |

Runtime errors (`RateLimitError`, `UpstreamError`, `PaginationLimitError`, …) are importable from `parse_apis` and can occur on any call.

> **Note.** Some params accept an enum whose corresponding output field is raw `str`/`list` (the wire value isn't bound to the enum). Enum members never compare equal to raw strings — compare such output values against `member.value`, or use plain string literals.
